# System space — Preview

```
$ navig space system

  SYSTEM  ·  OS & filesystem operator
  ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  agents      inspector · organizer · mover · converter
  skills      fs-inventory · file-organize · safe-move · long-path-ops
              dedupe · bulk-rename · convert · cleanup
  subspaces   media (transcode · OCR · A/V · image)
  doctrine    never hard-delete · verify by count · same-vol rename
              long-path \\?\ · purpose+size classify

  $ system inventory  "K:\Downloads"
    1,204 files · 18 dirs · 42.6 GB · 11 dupes · 3 zero-byte
  $ system size       "K:\DEV\BACKUP"
    10,706,065 files · 311 GB   (robocopy /L — 4s)
  $ system organize   "K:\Scripts" -To "E:\inspiration\scripts" -By purpose
    → 15 purpose buckets · INDEX.md · 0 lost · dry-run plan ready
  $ system migrate    "K:\_PROJECTS\gaze" -To "E:\projects\apps\gaze"
    copied ✓ verified ✓ (60 commits, 737 MB) → original → K:\.trash ✓
  $ system purge      "K:\.trash\DEV"
    long-path \\?\ delete · 8.49M files · /B for ACL locks · reclaimed 311 GB
```

# Bureau

Espace administratif français — gestion des documents officiels, impôts, logement, sécurité sociale, état civil, et correspondances avec les organismes publics et privés.

Langue par défaut : **français** (`default_locale: fr`). Les documents existent en version locale (`claim.fr.md`) ou bilingue (`claim.fr.md` + `claim.en.md`) selon le besoin.

---

## Structure

```
spaces/bureau/
  space.manifest.json     ← identité de l'espace
  README.md               ← ce fichier
  .navig\
    state\                ← contexte runtime
    plans\                ← phases administratives en cours
    memory\               ← contexte long-terme pour l'IA
  docs\                   ← documents de référence par domaine
  ops\                    ← runbooks et checklists administratives
  inbox\                  ← zone de dépôt : courriers à traiter
  out\                    ← documents envoyés, archivés, clôturés
```

---

## Espaces documentaires (domaines)

| Fichier | Domaine |
|---------|---------|
| [logement.md](logement.md) | Bail, charges, aides logement (APL), énergie, déménagements |

> Ajouter un domaine = créer un fichier `.md` dans ce dossier + une entrée dans ce tableau.

---

## Convention de nommage des fichiers

| Type | Convention | Exemple |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Document monolingue | `<nom>.<locale>.md` | `claim.fr.md` |
| Traduction | `<nom>.<locale>.md` | `claim.en.md` |
| Document sans locale spécifique | `<nom>.md` | `logement.md` (domaine entier) |

---

## Inbox — protocole de tri

1. Déposer tout courrier entrant (PDF, scan, email converti) dans `inbox/`
2. Classer dans `docs/<domaine>/` après traitement
3. Documents envoyés ou archivés → `out/`
4. Relances en attente → noter dans `.navig/plans/`

---

## Liens rapides

- Runbooks : `ops/README.md`
- Plans en cours : `.navig/plans/`
- Contexte IA : `.navig/memory/`

items.name: Social Circle

items.description: Your entire human network — mapped, searchable, and deeply personal.
items.author: navig-run
items.readme:
# Social Circle

> Your entire human network — mapped, searchable, and deeply personal.

Not a CRM. Not a social feed. A **personal relationship layer** — the one place where every person you know exists in one unified, living map.

---

## What It Does

Social Circle lets you maintain your full personal network across every dimension of your life:

| Dimension | Examples |
|-----------|---------|
| Real life | Close friends, family, neighbors, gym people |
| Work | Colleagues, clients, managers, ex-coworkers |
| Internet | Discord friends, Twitter mutuals, GitHub collaborators, forum regulars |
| Transient | Conference meets, one-time collaborators, warm leads |

You add people. You log how you're connected. You track when you last talked. The space tells you what's going cold and who you should reach out to.

---

## Core Features

### Circles
User-defined relationship buckets. Default set:

- **Close Friends** — deepest, most active
- **Family** — always in the graph
- **Work** — professional context
- **Online / Internet** — digital-first people
- **Acquaintances** — light-touch connections
- **Mentors & Advisors** — guidance relationships
- **Collaborators** — project-based partners
- **Archived** — dormant but preserved

Create, rename, merge, or delete circles at any time. One person can belong to multiple circles.

---

### Contacts
Each contact holds:

```
Name           Alice Mercer
Circles        Close Friends · Collaborators
Tags           met at DevCon 2024 · co-author · Berlin
Handles        @alicemercer (Twitter) · alicemercer (GitHub)
Last contact   2026-01-14 · Discord DM · discussed NAVIG launch
Strength       ████░ Strong (4/5)
Notes          Working on agent memory paper. Intro'd to Sam.
```

All fields are optional except name. Add what you know.

---

### Interaction Log
Lightweight touchpoint tracking per contact:

```
2026-03-12  voice call   Caught up post-launch. She's moving to Amsterdam.
2026-01-14  Discord DM   Discussed NAVIG memory architecture.
2025-11-03  IRL coffee   Met at FOSDEM Brussels. Talked open-source strategy.
```

Channels: `IRL` · `call` · `video` · `message` · `email` · `social` · `event` · `letter`

Log an interaction in one line: `navig contact log alice IRL coffee "discussed Amsterdam move"`

---

### Relationship Strength
Auto-calculated from interaction frequency. No manual scoring needed.

| Score | Label | When |
|-------|-------|------|
| ●●●●● | **Deep** | Multiple interactions / 30 days |
| ●●●●○ | **Strong** | Contacted in the last 90 days |
| ●●●○○ | **Active** | Contacted in the last 6 months |
| ●●○○○ | **Warm** | Contacted in the last 12 months |
| ●○○○○ | **Cold** | 12+ months since last interaction |
| ○○○○○ | **Dormant** | Never logged |

The agent surfaces all Cold and Dormant contacts on demand: "Who have I not talked to in a year?"

---

### Visual Graph View
Force-directed node graph. Every contact is a node. Circles define clusters. Edge thickness = relationship strength.

Interactive:
- Click a node → contact detail drawer
- Drag to rearrange clusters
- Filter by circle, tag, or strength
- Highlight mutual connections between contacts

---

### List & Card View
- **List** — sortable table: name, circles, tags, last interaction, strength
- **Card** — grid of contact cards with photo/avatar, circle badges, last-contact indicator

Toggle freely. Both views share the same filter state.

---

### Search & Filter
Full-text search across names, tags, notes, and handles.

Filter combinations:
```
circle:Work AND strength:Cold
tag:"met at" AND last_contact:>2025-01-01
circle:Mentors
handle:github:*
```

---

## Import

| Source | How |
|--------|-----|
| Manual | Type directly or via quick-add form |
| CSV | Any CSV — agent maps columns on import |
| LinkedIn | Export `Connections.csv` from LinkedIn Data → drop in inbox |
| Google Contacts | `.vcf` or Google CSV export |
| Twitter/X | Paste a handle — agent resolves name + bio |
| vCard (`.vcf`) | Standard contact files |

All imports land in `.navig/inbox/` for review before committing to the graph.

---

## Packages

| Package | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| `contact-graph` | Core data model — contacts, circles, connections, strength engine |
| `circle-manager` | Circle CRUD, membership management, merge/split |
| `interaction-log` | Touchpoint logging, channel types, timeline queries |
| `import-bridge` | CSV/VCF/LinkedIn/Google import pipeline with field mapping |
| `relationship-strength` | Frequency-based strength calculator, cold-contact surfacing |

---

## Agent Capabilities

Ask the agent anything about your network:

```
"Who haven't I talked to in 6 months?"
"Add Sofia Kovac — Discord friend, online circle, met in the NAVIG server"
"Log a call with Marcus yesterday, we discussed the Berlin trip"
"Show me everyone I know at Stripe"
"Who introduced me to Jake?"
"Generate a summary of my relationship with Alice"
"My Work circle — who's gone cold?"
"Import this LinkedIn CSV and match duplicates"
```

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# Load the space
navig space load social-circle-space

# Add your first contact
navig contact add "Alice Mercer" --circle "Close Friends" --tag "met at DevCon 2024"

# Log an interaction
navig contact log alice call "caught up, she's moving to Amsterdam"

# Open the graph
navig graph open

# Find cold contacts
navig contacts --filter strength:cold

# Import from LinkedIn
cp ~/Downloads/Connections.csv .navig/inbox/
navig wiki inbox process
```

---

## Setup

```bash
# Linux / macOS — create optional root symlinks
bash setup-links.sh

# Windows
powershell setup-links.ps1
```

---

*Social Circle — NAVIG OS · core tier · `crossplatform: true`*

Personal finance command layer — budget, cashflow, savings goals, investments, and tax preparation.

```bash
# Initialize your first account
cp accounts/_template/account.json accounts/checking.json

# Import transactions for this month
@budget-analyst import --account checking --file transactions.csv

# Run monthly spending report
@budget-analyst report --month current

# Check savings goals progress
@savings-coach progress

# Get investment portfolio summary
@investment-tracker summary

# Start tax prep checklist
@tax-planner checklist --year 2025
```

## Space Structure

```
finance-space/
  accounts/          One JSON file per account (bank, investment, retirement, credit)
  transactions/      Monthly CSVs: {YYYY-MM}/{account}.csv
  budgets/           Category targets: {YYYY}/budget.json + monthly actuals
  goals/             savings-goals.json, debt-payoff.json
  documents/
    tax/{YYYY}/      Tax documents organized by year
    statements/      Account statements archive
  reports/           Generated reports (monthly close, tax summaries)

| `budget-analyst` | Tracks spending, variance analysis, monthly close | #budget |
| `investment-tracker` | Portfolio holdings, returns, rebalancing | #investments |
| `tax-planner` | Tax estimates, deduction tracking, filing prep | #taxes |
| `savings-coach` | Goal progress, savings rate, milestone alerts | #goals |

| Workflow | When | What it does |

| `monthly-close` | 1st of month | Variance analysis + savings update |
| `weekly-spending` | Every Monday | Spending pace vs budget |
| `tax-prep-checklist` | Jan–Apr | Document checklist + estimate |

## Transaction CSV Format

date,description,amount,category,account,notes
2026-03-01,Grocery store,-85.40,food,checking,weekly shop

# Travel Space

Turn any trip idea into a well-planned, well-documented adventure.
Handles everything from rough estimate to debrief.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Create a new trip
navig flow run new-trip

# Check pre-departure checklist
navig flow run pre-departure --trip tokyo-2026

# Debrief after returning
navig flow run trip-debrief --trip tokyo-2026
```

## Structure

```
trips/
  {slug}/
    trip.json        Trip metadata: dates, destination, budget, status
    itinerary.md     Day-by-day plan
    budget.json      Estimated vs actual costs
    bookings/        Flight, hotel, activity confirmations
    documents/       Visa, insurance, tickets (local copies)
    notes/           Research, recommendations, on-trip notes
    debrief.md       Post-trip retrospective
```

## Agents

| Agent | What It Does |
|-------|-------------|
| trip-planner | Creates and manages trip structure, cost estimates |
| itinerary-builder | Builds day-by-day schedule, suggests activities |
| budget-watcher | Tracks bookings vs budget, flags overruns |
| document-keeper | Manages trip documents, pre-departure checklist |

## Workflows

| Workflow | When |
|----------|------|
| new-trip | When you decide on a destination |
| pre-departure | 1–7 days before travel |
| trip-debrief | Within 48 hours of returning |

## Inbox Routes

- `#trip-ideas` — rough idea, not yet committed
- `#active-trip` — current or upcoming confirmed trip
- `#bookings` — confirmation numbers, itinerary PDFs

| Domain | What it covers |
|--------|---------------|
| **Clients** | Client registry, tiers, rates, relationship status |
| **Projects** | Deliverables, milestones, budget caps, scope health |
| **Time** | Billable and non-billable time log per project and client |
| **Invoices** | Draft → sent → paid lifecycle with overdue alerting |

## Quick Start

```bash

# War Room — Operator Command Center 🛰️

> **OSINT · Investigation · Ethical Hacking.** Find, investigate, and operate from one
> command center — open-source intelligence, structured case-work, attack-surface mapping,
> authorized red-team ops, digital forensics, and an isolated lab. Every operation is **gated
> by written authorization and rules of engagement** (see [Prime Directive](#prime-directive)).

See [`.navig/context.md`](.navig/context.md) for the full doctrine.

## Prime Directive
**No collection, recon, scanning, or exploitation against a target without standing
authorization for that target.** Passive/open sources by default; scope is a fence; minimize
and protect subject data; the dangerous parts happen in the isolated `lab/`; responsible
disclosure always. The `legal-counsel` agent owns this gate — see
[`docs/ETHICS-AND-AUTHORIZATION.md`](docs/ETHICS-AND-AUTHORIZATION.md).

## Agents
| Agent | Theater | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `strategist` | command | War picture across theaters, tasking, priorities (lead) |
| `osint-analyst` | OSINT | Open-source collection, entity enrichment, the graph |
| `recon-operator` | recon | Authorized footprinting + attack-surface mapping |
| `red-team-lead` | offense | Authorized ethical-hacking engagements (ATT&CK), the lab |
| `forensics-investigator` | DFIR | Evidence, artifacts, chain of custody, timelines |
| `case-manager` | investigation | Owns cases end-to-end; the final intelligence report |
| `intelligence-officer` | intel | Adversary tracking, IOC/TTP, signal reliability |
| `legal-counsel` | legal/ethics | The authorization gate — scope, RoE, legality, disclosure |
| `narrative-engineer` | narrative | Comms, counter-narrative, disinformation tracing |

## Skills
| Skill | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `open-case` | Open an investigation (subject, objective, scope, authorization) |
| `add-entity` | Add a node to the OSINT graph (person/org/domain/ip/email/handle/wallet) |
| `log-finding` | Log a corroborated finding (confidence, source, evidence ref) |
| `map-asset` | Register a discovered asset in the attack-surface registry (scoped) |
| `start-engagement` | Open an **authorized** red-team engagement (scope + RoE + auth ref) — gated |
| `build-op` · `advance-status` | Create / advance an operation (planning → active → hold → closed) |
| `log-intel` · `arsenal-search` | Log a signal · search the arsenal |

## Formations
`ops-command` (default) · `osint-sweep` · `recon-and-map` · `investigation` · `red-team-op` (gated) · `intel-sweep` · `narrative-war`

## Pipelines
```
Investigation:    open-case → collect → enrich graph → corroborate → findings → report
Recon (authz):    authorize → footprint → map surface → prioritize → findings → disclose
Red-team (authz): scope+RoE → recon → plan(ATT&CK) → execute-in-scope → evidence → report
Operation spine:  planning → active → hold → closed | aborted
```

## Data plane (`.navig/memory/`)
`cases.json` · `entities.json` (graph) · `findings.json` · `assets.json` (attack surface) ·
`iocs.json` · `engagements.json` (authorized) · `adversaries.json` · `operations.json` ·
`intel-log.json` · `arsenal-registry.json`

## Arsenal & lab
```
arsenal/osint  recon  cyber  forensic  legal  verbal  marketing      lab/  (isolated range — see lab/README.md)
```

## Connections (MCP)
OSINT sources, scanners, the browser, the case DB, and the lab are wired as MCP servers /
registered connections — see [`.navig/store/mcp/`](.navig/store/mcp/) and
[`arsenal/CONNECTIONS.md`](arsenal/CONNECTIONS.md).

## Prompt arsenal

items.readme:
# Research Space

> Turn open questions into trustworthy data. Search the web, crawl and extract,
> build datasets at scale, store them in a database, and synthesize cited findings.

**Owner:** navig-run
**Created:** 2026-06-15
**Status:** active
**Runtime:** navig-space-2

---

## What This Is

Research Space is a **discovery-to-data pipeline**. It exists for the work that
starts with "I need to know X" and ends with a clean, queryable dataset and a
finding you can defend. Discover new information on the web, crawl it into
structured records, deduplicate and normalize it into datasets, load it into a
database that scales, and query it for answers — each step with provenance.

```
question → [scout] search & track → [crawler] crawl & extract
         → [curator] normalize & dedupe → [archivist] store in DB
         → [analyst] query & synthesize → cited findings
```

## Agents

| Agent | Role |
|-------|------|
| `scout` | Web search, source discovery and evaluation, source tracking |
| `crawler` | Crawling and structured extraction (lists, tables, pagination) |
| `curator` | Normalization, deduplication, schema validation, dataset building |
| `archivist` | Database schema, ingestion, indexing, health at scale |
| `analyst` | Querying, pattern-finding, cited synthesis, research briefs |

## Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `web-search` | Run a search and record ranked candidate sources |
| `track-source` | Promote a source to monitored + recrawled on an interval |
| `crawl-site` | Crawl a source and stage raw records to `crawls/*.jsonl` |
| `build-dataset` | Merge, normalize, dedupe → `datasets/*.json` and load into SQLite |
| `db-query` | Run a read-only SQL query against the research database |

## Formations

| Formation | Lead | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `discovery-run` | scout | Default — find new info and track credible sources |
| `crawl-pipeline` | crawler | Crawl tracked sources into raw records |
| `data-foundry` | curator | Build datasets and store them in the database |
| `analysis-lab` | analyst | Query the data and synthesize cited findings |

## Workflows

| Workflow | Schedule | Purpose |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `daily-discovery-sweep` | daily 07:00 | Search active topics, recrawl due sources |
| `weekly-research-review` | Sun 08:00 | Dataset health, new findings, stale topics |

## Layout

```
research/
├── .navig/              ← agents, skills, formations, workflows, memory, config
├── crawls/              ← raw staged extractions (*.jsonl) — regenerable, gitignored
├── datasets/            ← canonical, deduplicated datasets (*.json)
├── out/                 ← research.db and generated outputs
├── scripts/             ← helper scripts
└── README.md
```

## Quick Start

```bash
# 1. Start a topic — Scout searches and tracks sources
navig skill run web-search --query "open EV charging datasets Europe" --topic ev-stations
navig skill run track-source --url https://example.org/data --topic ev-stations

# 2. Crawl a source into staging
navig skill run crawl-site --url https://example.org/data --dataset ev-stations

# 3. Build the dataset and load it into the database
navig skill run build-dataset --dataset ev-stations --key id

# 4. Ask a question
navig skill run db-query --sql "SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM 'ev-stations' GROUP BY country"
```

> Search and fetch backends are pluggable via MCP (`.navig/store/mcp/workstation.mcp.json`).
> Bind one before expecting live results — the skills stage and log runs regardless.

---

*Bootstrap guide for AI agents: [`GENESIS.md`](GENESIS.md) · Context: [`.navig/context.md`](.navig/context.md)*

items.readme:
# devtools-space

A navig space of **developer shell tools** for Windows. One PowerShell engine
(`bin/devtools.ps1`) backs three surfaces from a single place:

1. **`navig skill run`** — e.g. `navig skill run compress extract-folder --target "C:\dl"`
2. **The AI agent** — every tool is a skill, callable via the agent's `skill_run` tool
3. **The Windows right-click menu** — installed from `bin/menu.manifest.json`

Modeled on `media-space` (engine + `Common.ps1` + `.navig/skills/*.yaml`).

## Layout

```
bin/
  devtools.ps1          unified engine (dispatch on the first arg)
  DevTools-Common.ps1   shared helpers: UI (no brackets), Find-Tool, coalescing
  run-hidden.vbs        windowless launcher (no console flash on multi-select)
  menu.manifest.json    single source of truth for the right-click menu
  menu/
    install.ps1         deploy engine + register HKCU verbs (no admin)
    uninstall.ps1       remove the menu
    migrate-from-programdata.ps1   retire the old C:\ProgramData\DevToolkit (admin, one-time)
.navig/
  config.yaml           space config (engine, skills_dir, safety)
  skills/*.yaml         one skill per tool group (CLI + agent surface)
config.example.json     ssh / VirusTotal config template -> copy to config.json
```

## Tools

| Skill | Commands |
|-------|----------|
| compress | extract-here, extract-folder, zip, 7z, 7z-split, open |
| git-clone | clone, open-repo |
| copy-structure | copy-tree, copy-folders, copy-files, copy-sizes, copy-contents |
| download | video, image |
| dev | npm, docker |
| remote | ssh, upload, deploy |
| scan | virustotal |
| url | shorten |
| unlock | unlock (find lockers via Restart Manager, kill, take ownership, clear attrs, delete) |
| shell-menu | install, uninstall, migrate, doctor |

## Install the right-click menu

```powershell
# from this space:
pwsh bin\menu\install.ps1            # deploy + register (HKCU, no admin)
pwsh bin\menu\install.ps1 -DryRun    # preview
pwsh bin\menu\install.ps1 -List      # what's registered
pwsh bin\menu\uninstall.ps1          # remove
pwsh bin\menu\migrate-from-programdata.ps1   # one-time: drop legacy HKLM menu (admin)
```

Or via navig: `navig skill run shell-menu install` / `uninstall` / `migrate` / `doctor`.

### Multi-select, one window

Explorer fires a `%1` verb once per selected file. The compress verbs launch
through `run-hidden.vbs` (truly windowless), and the engine **coalesces** those
per-file invocations into ONE visible worker window via a queue + leader-election
mutex. Select 20 archives -> one terminal, each extracted to its own folder — not
20 windows.

## Add or edit a tool (for humans and the AI)

1. Add a `switch` branch in `bin/devtools.ps1` (use `Write-Step/Ok/Warn/Err` from
   `DevTools-Common.ps1` — no bracket tags).
2. Add a `.navig/skills/<group>.yaml` command entry with `agent_hints`.
3. To surface it in the right-click menu, add an item to `bin/menu.manifest.json`
   and re-run `install`.

All three are plain text/JSON/YAML — reviewable diffs, no build step.

items.name: Extract Entities
items.tagline: Extract named entities (people, places, orgs, dates) from any text
items.description: Extract named entities (people, places, orgs, dates) from any text
items.readme:
# Purpose

Extract named entities — people, organisations, locations, dates, products, technologies, and events — from any text. Returns structured JSON with position offsets and confidence scores.

# When to use

- User has text and wants to know who, what, where, or when is mentioned
- Pipeline step for analysis tasks (contract review, news parsing, log triage)
- Trigger type: agent task type `analysis` or pipeline step

# Instructions

1. Only extract entities explicitly present in the text
2. Flag ambiguous entities with `confidence < 0.7`
3. Return character-level `start`/`end` offsets for each entity
4. If no entities of a requested type are found, return an empty array for that type (do not omit the key)
5. Detect language automatically; note if non-English

# Inputs

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `text` | string | yes | — |
| `entity_types` | array of strings | no | `["person", "organization", "location", "date"]` |

Valid entity types: `person`, `organization`, `location`, `date`, `product`, `technology`, `event`, `custom`

# Output format

```json
{
  "entities": [
    {
      "text":       "Elon Musk",
      "type":       "person",
      "confidence": 0.97,
      "start":      0,
      "end":        9
    }
  ],
  "entity_count":      3,
  "language_detected": "en"
}
```

# Examples

```bash
# Extract all default entity types from text
navig skill run extract-entities --text "Apple announced Tim Cook will visit Berlin on Friday."

# Extract only people and organisations
navig skill run extract-entities \
  --text "OpenAI and Google DeepMind published competing papers." \
  --entity_types '["person","organization"]'
```

# Agent hints

After extraction, offer to cross-reference entities against a knowledge base or perform sentiment analysis per entity.
If `confidence < 0.7` for any entity, mention it to the user as uncertain.

items.tagline: Fetch and summarise any URL in configurable length and format
items.description: Fetch and summarise any URL in configurable length and format
items.readme:
# Purpose

Fetch a URL and return a structured summary of its content — title, key points, and a concise prose summary. Preserves factual accuracy over brevity.

# When to use

- User shares a URL and asks for a summary, overview, or key takeaways
- User says "summarise this", "what's on this page", "tldr for this link"
- Trigger type: `/summarise` command or agent task type `research`

# Instructions

1. Fetch the URL content (use browser rendering if JS-gated)
2. Extract: page title, main body text, key entities and figures
3. Produce a concise summary (default max 300 words, configurable)
4. List 3–5 key points as bullet points
5. Flag if the content is paywalled, empty, or non-textual
6. Never fabricate details — only use what is on the page

# Inputs

| Field | Type | Required | Default |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `url` | string (URI) | yes | — |
| `max_length` | integer (words) | no | 300 |

# Output format

```json
{
  "title":      "Page Title",
  "summary":    "Concise prose summary...",
  "key_points": ["Point one", "Point two", "Point three"],
  "source_url": "https://example.com/article"
}
```

# Examples

```bash
# Summarise an article
/summarise https://example.com/blog/new-feature

# With a custom word limit
navig skill run summarise-url --url https://docs.example.com --max_length 150
```

# Agent hints

After summarising, offer to extract named entities, translate, or generate a social post from the summary.
If the page is paywalled, offer to search for an archive or alternative source.

items.name: Cloudflare
items.tagline: Router for the whole Cloudflare platform — picks the right product and hands off to a focused skill
items.description: Router for the whole Cloudflare platform — picks the right product and hands off to a focused skill
items.readme:
# Cloudflare — platform router

Pick the right Cloudflare primitive, then hand off. This skill routes; the sibling skills below do
the work. It does not deploy anything by itself.

**Trust the docs over memory.** Cloudflare limits, pricing, binding shapes, and compatibility flags
change often, and your training may be stale. Before quoting a number or an API signature, retrieve:

| Source | Where | Use for |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Cloudflare docs | `https://developers.cloudflare.com/` | Limits, pricing, API reference, compat dates |
| Wrangler schema | `node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json` | Exact binding shapes + allowed config fields |
| Workers types | `npm pack @cloudflare/workers-types` | Handler + binding type signatures |
| Changelog | `https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/` | Recent deprecations and limit changes |

When a reference and the live docs disagree, the docs win — especially for numeric limits, pricing,
and type signatures.

## Where Cloudflare already lives in navig

Before adding a new pattern, look at how navig already ships on Cloudflare — reuse the seam:

- `services/api/` — the `api.navig.run` Worker (Hono + D1): billing, licensing, marketplace. The
  reference for a real production Worker in this tree.
- `services/lighthouse/` — the self-hosted edge Worker (outbound WS uplink, **no tunnel**). Built with
  `cd services/lighthouse && npm run build:bundle` → a prebuilt `worker.js` the Python deployer uploads.
- `core/navig/cloud/deck_deploy.py` + `core/navig/cloud/cf_oauth.py` — navig deploys Workers/Static
  Assets **via the Cloudflare REST API from pure Python** (Wrangler-style PKCE OAuth or a scoped API
  token). No `wrangler` binary is needed at deploy time. If you are building operator-side deploy
  automation, extend these — do not shell out to wrangler.

## Decision trees

### Run code
```
Serverless HTTP at the edge          → Workers        (skill: workers-best-practices, wrangler)
Full-stack app with Git deploys      → Pages
Stateful coordination / real-time    → Durable Objects (skill: durable-objects)
Long-running multi-step jobs         → Workflows
Stateful AI agent (chat/tools/MCP)   → Agents SDK      (skill: cloudflare-agents)
Run/isolate untrusted or LLM code    → Sandbox SDK     (skill: cloudflare-sandbox)
Run containers                       → Containers
Scheduled tasks (cron)               → Cron Triggers
```

### Store data
```
Key-value (config, sessions, cache)  → KV
Relational SQL                       → D1 (SQLite)  ·  Hyperdrive (front an existing Postgres/MySQL)
Object / file storage (S3-compatible)→ R2
Async message queue                  → Queues
Vector embeddings (RAG / search)     → Vectorize
Per-entity strongly-consistent state → Durable Objects storage (skill: durable-objects)
Secrets                              → Secrets Store  ·  per-Worker: wrangler secret put
```

### AI / ML
```
Run inference (LLMs, embeddings)     → Workers AI
Vector DB for RAG                    → Vectorize
Build a stateful agent               → Agents SDK   (skill: cloudflare-agents)
One gateway across AI providers      → AI Gateway
```

### Networking · Security · Other
```
Expose a local service (no port fwd) → Tunnel
TCP/UDP (non-HTTP) proxy             → Spectrum
WAF / DDoS / bot / API protection    → WAF · DDoS · Bot Management · API Shield
CAPTCHA alternative                  → Turnstile
Transactional email (send/receive)   → Email Service (skill: cloudflare-email)
Images / video / browser rendering   → Images · Stream · Browser Rendering
Analytics across products            → GraphQL Analytics API · Analytics Engine · Workers Logs
Infra as code                        → Terraform · Pulumi · REST API
```

## Sibling skills — load the specific one

| You are doing… | Load |
|----------------|------|
| Running `wrangler` commands / editing `wrangler.jsonc` | `wrangler` |
| Writing or reviewing Worker code | `workers-best-practices` |
| Stateful coordination, WebSockets, per-entity state | `durable-objects` |
| A chat/tool/MCP AI agent on Workers | `cloudflare-agents` |
| Sending or receiving email | `cloudflare-email` |
| Executing untrusted or LLM-generated code | `cloudflare-sandbox` |

## Operator defaults

- Prefer **in-process bindings** (KV/D1/R2/Queues) over the Cloudflare REST API from inside a Worker.
- Prefer **`wrangler.jsonc`** over TOML — newer features are JSON-only.
- Keep a recent `compatibility_date`; enable `nodejs_compat` when a dependency needs Node built-ins.
- Secrets go through `wrangler secret put` / Secrets Store — **never** inline in config or source.
- Deploys are mutating and target a real account. Confirm the environment (`staging` vs `production`)
  before `wrangler deploy`; dry-run first (`wrangler deploy --dry-run`).

items.name: Wrangler
items.tagline: Cloudflare Workers CLI — deploy, dev, and manage Workers, KV, R2, D1, Queues, secrets
items.description: Cloudflare Workers CLI — deploy, dev, and manage Workers, KV, R2, D1, Queues, secrets
items.readme:
# Wrangler CLI

Wrangler flags, config fields, and subcommands change between majors. **Retrieve before you commit
to a command.** Sources: `https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/` and the local schema
`node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json` (exact binding shapes + allowed values).

> **navig reality check.** navig's *product* deploys (edge Worker, deck) go through **pure-Python
> Cloudflare REST calls** — `core/navig/cloud/deck_deploy.py` + `cf_oauth.py` — so end users never
> install wrangler. You use wrangler here for **local dev and the TypeScript Workers in the repo**
> (`services/api`, `services/lighthouse`). Do not add a wrangler dependency to the operator install
> path; keep deploy automation on the existing Python REST seam.

## First: is it installed?

```bash
wrangler --version      # needs v4.x+
npm install -D wrangler@latest   # if missing — pin to the repo, not global
```

Prefer wrangler over hand-built REST requests for local/CI work.

## Core commands

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Local dev server | `wrangler dev` |
| Deploy | `wrangler deploy` |
| Validate without deploying | `wrangler deploy --dry-run` |
| Deploy an environment | `wrangler deploy --env staging` |
| Generate TS binding types | `wrangler types` |
| Profile startup (CPU limit) | `wrangler check startup` |
| Live logs | `wrangler tail --status error` |
| Who am I / auth | `wrangler whoami` · `wrangler login` |
| List / view / roll back versions | `wrangler versions list` · `wrangler rollback [<id>]` |

**Auth in CI:** set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (scoped: *Workers Scripts: Edit*) rather than an
interactive `wrangler login`. Never echo the token.

## wrangler.jsonc (prefer JSONC over TOML)

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",
  "name": "my-worker",
  "main": "src/index.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-01-01",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "observability": { "enabled": true, "head_sampling_rate": 1 },

  "vars": { "ENVIRONMENT": "production" },
  "kv_namespaces":  [{ "binding": "KV",  "id": "<KV_ID>" }],
  "r2_buckets":     [{ "binding": "BUCKET", "bucket_name": "my-bucket" }],
  "d1_databases":   [{ "binding": "DB", "database_name": "my-db", "database_id": "<DB_ID>", "migrations_dir": "./migrations" }],
  "ai": { "binding": "AI" },
  "durable_objects": { "bindings": [{ "name": "ROOM", "class_name": "Room" }] },
  "queues": { "producers": [{ "binding": "Q", "queue": "jobs" }] },
  "triggers": { "crons": ["0 * * * *"] },

  "env": {
    "staging": { "name": "my-worker-staging", "vars": { "ENVIRONMENT": "staging" } }
  }
}
```

After any binding change: `wrangler types` (regenerate `Env`) — never hand-write binding interfaces.

## Resource management (one line each)

```bash
wrangler kv namespace create MY_KV
wrangler r2 bucket create my-bucket
wrangler d1 create my-db
wrangler d1 migrations apply my-db --remote      # --local for the dev copy
wrangler d1 execute my-db --remote --command "SELECT 1"   # --remote hits prod data
wrangler vectorize create idx --dimensions 768 --metric cosine
wrangler queues create jobs
wrangler pages deploy ./dist --project-name my-site
```

Omit resource IDs to let wrangler auto-provision on first deploy.

## Secrets — never on the command line

```bash
wrangler secret put API_KEY               # interactive prompt (preferred)
wrangler secret put PRIVATE_KEY < key.pem # from a file (PEM / CI)
wrangler secret list
```

Do **not** pass secret values as arguments, `echo` them, or commit `.dev.vars`. For local dev put
non-production secrets in `.dev.vars` (gitignored). This mirrors navig's rule: secrets go through
the vault, never a tracked file.

## Local dev notes

- Bindings default to **local simulation**; add `"remote": true` on a binding to hit the real
  resource. Workers AI is **always** remote and bills even locally.
- Test cron: `wrangler dev --test-scheduled` then `curl http://localhost:8787/__scheduled`.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| `command not found: wrangler` | `npm install -D wrangler@latest` |
| Auth errors | `wrangler login` (or set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) |
| Binding `undefined` in Worker | Binding name must match config **exactly**; re-run `wrangler types` |
| Startup-time limit exceeded | `wrangler check startup` to profile |
| Local state stale | inspect `.wrangler/state` |

items.description: Author and review Cloudflare Workers code against production best practices and anti-patterns
items.readme:
# Workers — best practices & review

Worker code in examples gets pasted straight into production. Be certain: **retrieve before you
flag.** Canonical rules live at
`https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/best-practices/workers-best-practices/`; exact type
signatures come from `@cloudflare/workers-types` (`npm pack` for the latest), config shapes from
`node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json`.

navig's real Workers are the reference implementations to match: `services/api/` (Hono + D1) and
`services/lighthouse/` (the edge uplink Worker). Review new Worker code against how those handle
bindings, errors, and observability.

## Review workflow

1. **Retrieve** — latest best-practices page + workers types + wrangler schema.
2. **Read whole files**, not just the diff — binding access and global state need surrounding context.
3. **Types** — no `any` on `Env` or handlers, no `as unknown as T` double-casts; `Env` is generated
   by `wrangler types`, never hand-written.
4. **Config** — `compatibility_date`, `nodejs_compat`, `observability`, secrets, and binding names
   matching the code.
5. **Patterns** — streaming, floating promises, request-scoped global state.
6. **Security** — crypto source, secret handling, timing-safe comparisons, explicit error responses.
7. **Validate** — `npx tsc --noEmit`; lint for `no-floating-promises`.

## The rules (correct pattern → why)

| Rule | Do this |
|------|---------|
| **Stream large/unknown payloads** | Pipe the body; never `await response.text()` on unbounded data (128 MB memory ceiling). |
| **`ctx.waitUntil()` for post-response work** | And **don't destructure `ctx`** — `const { waitUntil } = ctx` loses `this` and throws "Illegal invocation". |
| **Bindings over REST** | Use in-process KV/R2/D1/Queues bindings, not the Cloudflare REST API from inside a Worker. |
| **Service bindings for Worker→Worker** | Not a public HTTPS round-trip. |
| **Hyperdrive for external PG/MySQL** | Always front an external SQL DB with Hyperdrive. |
| **`extends`, not `implements`** | On `DurableObject` / `WorkerEntrypoint` / `Workflow` — `implements` loses `this.ctx` / `this.env`. Inside those classes use `this.env.X`, not `env.X`. |
| **Web Crypto for anything security-bearing** | `crypto.randomUUID()` / `crypto.getRandomValues()`; compare secrets with `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual`. |
| **Explicit try/catch + structured errors** | Not `ctx.passThroughOnException()` as error handling. |
| **Structured JSON logs + observability** | Enable `observability` with a `head_sampling_rate`. |
| **Move async work off the critical path** | Queues / Workflows for background jobs. |

## Anti-patterns to flag

| Anti-pattern | Why it bites |
|--------------|--------------|
| `await response.text()` on unbounded data | Memory exhaustion at the 128 MB limit. |
| Hardcoded secrets in source or config | Leaked through version control. |
| `Math.random()` for tokens/IDs | Predictable — not cryptographically secure. |
| Bare `fetch()` with no `await`/`waitUntil` | Floating promise: dropped result, swallowed error. |
| Module-level mutable vars for request state | Cross-request leaks, stale reads, I/O errors. |
| Cloudflare REST API from inside a Worker | Needless hop + auth overhead + latency. |
| Direct `===` on secret values | Timing side-channel — use `timingSafeEqual`. |
| Hand-written `Env` interface | Drifts from actual wrangler bindings. |
| `ctx.passThroughOnException()` as a catch | Hides bugs; undebuggable. |

## Principles

- **Provide evidence** — cite line numbers, tool output, or a docs link, not a vibe.
- **Correctness over completeness** — a short example that runs beats a broad one with errors.
- Adjacent skills: `durable-objects` (stateful/WebSocket), `wrangler` (CLI/config),
  `cloudflare-agents` (agent framework), `cloudflare-email` (email). Workflows rules:
  `https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/rules-of-workflows/`.

items.readme:
# Cloudflare Agents SDK

> **Name note:** this covers the *Cloudflare* `agents` package (Durable-Object-backed agents on
> Workers). It is unrelated to navig's own agents, formations, and `.github/agents/`. Don't conflate
> the two — an `Agent` class here is a Cloudflare DO, not a navig subagent.

Each agent is a Durable Object with a class instance per name: persistent state, its own SQLite,
WebSocket connections, and a scheduler. **Prefer retrieval over memory** — the API surface is large
and evolving: `https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/` (per-topic pages under
`/api-reference/`). Fetch the specific page when implementing a feature.

## What it gives you

Persistent auto-synced state (`setState`) · callable RPC (`@callable`) · scheduling (once /
`scheduleEvery` / cron) · durable Workflows (`AgentWorkflow`) · durable execution (`runFiber` /
`stash`, survives eviction) · built-in FIFO queue + `retry()` with backoff · MCP client **and**
server (`McpAgent`) · streaming chat (`AIChatAgent`, resumable) · React hooks (`useAgent`,
`useAgentChat`) · email handling · webhooks + push · diagnostics-channel observability.

## First: install

```bash
npm ls agents || npm install agents
# chat agents also need:
npm install agents @cloudflare/ai-chat ai @ai-sdk/react
```

## wrangler config

```jsonc
{
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "durable_objects": { "bindings": [{ "name": "MyAgent", "class_name": "MyAgent" }] },
  "migrations": [{ "tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["MyAgent"] }],
  "ai": { "binding": "AI" }
}
```

**Gotchas:** do NOT enable `experimentalDecorators` in tsconfig (breaks `@callable`); never edit an
old migration tag; each agent class needs its own binding + migration entry.

## The agent class

```typescript
import { Agent, routeAgentRequest, callable } from "agents";

type State = { count: number };

export class Counter extends Agent<Env, State> {
  initialState = { count: 0 };

  validateStateChange(next: State) {
    if (next.count < 0) throw new Error("Count cannot be negative");
  }

  @callable()
  increment() {
    this.setState({ count: this.state.count + 1 });
    return this.state.count;
  }
}

export default {
  fetch: (req, env) => routeAgentRequest(req, env) ?? new Response("Not found", { status: 404 }),
};
```

**Routing:** requests map to `/agents/{agent-name}/{instance-name}` (e.g. `Counter` →
`/agents/counter/user-123`). Custom: `getAgentByName(env.MyAgent, "id")` then `agent.fetch(request)`.

## Core APIs

| Task | API |
|------|-----|
| Read / write state | `this.state.x` · `this.setState({ x })` |
| SQL | `` this.sql`SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ${id}` `` |
| Schedule (delay / cron / interval) | `this.schedule(60, "task", p)` · `this.schedule("0 * * * *", …)` · `this.scheduleEvery(30, "poll")` |
| RPC / streaming RPC | `@callable() m()` · `@callable({ streaming: true }) s(res)` |
| Workflow / durable fiber | `this.runWorkflow("W", p)` · `this.runFiber("n", async ctx => …)` |
| Queue / retry | `this.queue("handler", p)` · `this.retry(fn, { maxAttempts: 5 })` |
| Broadcast / connections | `this.broadcast(msg)` · `this.getConnections(tag?)` |

## React client

```tsx
import { useAgent } from "agents/react";

const agent = useAgent({
  agent: "Counter",
  name: "my-instance",
  onStateUpdate: (s) => setLocalState(s),
});
// agent.setState({ count: state.count + 1 })
```

## When you want more depth (fetch the doc)

| Topic | Docs page |
|-------|-----------|
| State & sync | `/agents/api-reference/store-and-sync-state/` |
| Callable / streaming RPC | `/agents/api-reference/callable-methods/` |
| Scheduling | `/agents/api-reference/schedule-tasks/` |
| Workflows / durable execution | `/agents/api-reference/run-workflows/` · `/durable-execution/` |
| Queue / retries | `/agents/api-reference/queue-tasks/` · `/retries/` |
| Chat agents (AIChatAgent) | `/agents/api-reference/chat-agents/` |
| Client SDK (hooks) | `/agents/api-reference/client-sdk/` |
| MCP client / server | `/agents/api-reference/mcp-client-api/` · `/mcp-agent-api/` · securing: `/securing-mcp-servers/` |
| Email / webhooks / push | `/agents/api-reference/email/` · `/webhooks/` · `/push-notifications/` |
| Observability | `/agents/api-reference/observability/` |

Adjacent skills: `durable-objects` (the substrate), `workers-best-practices`, `cloudflare-email`
(the agent `onEmail` path), `wrangler`.

items.description: Send and receive transactional email with Cloudflare Email Service (Workers binding, REST, routing)
items.readme:
# Cloudflare Email Service Send transactional email and route inbound email inside Cloudflare. **The docs are source of truth** (the product is new and moving): `https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/`, REST spec at `https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/email_sending`. If this skill and the docs disagree, the docs win. > **navig context.** navig's own product-level email lives in the **`navig-email`** plugin — that is > the operator-facing "send/inbox" surface. This skill is different: it's for *building on Cloudflare > Email Service inside a Worker or agent* (e.g. the `services/api` Worker sending a receipt, or a > Cloudflare agent replying to inbound mail). Transactional messages only — route newsletters and > campaigns through a dedicated marketing platform. ## First: prerequisites 1. **Domain onboarded?** `npx wrangler email sending list`. If missing: `npx wrangler email sending enable yourdomain.com` (or the Dashboard). 2. **Binding present?** `send_email` in `wrangler.jsonc` (Workers path). 3. **Parsing inbound?** `npm ls postal-mime` (only for receiving). ## Path picker | You want to… | Path | |--------------|------| | Send from a **Worker** | `send_email` binding — no API keys. **Recommended.** | | Send from a **Cloudflare agent** | `onEmail()` + `replyToEmail()` in the Agent class. | | Send from an **external app** (Node/Go/Python) | REST API with a Bearer token. | | **Receive / route** incoming mail | Worker `email()` handler. | | Set up sending or routing | `wrangler email sending enable` / `wrangler email routing enable`. | ## Send — Workers binding (preferred) ```jsonc // wrangler.jsonc { "send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }] } ``` ```typescript await env.EMAIL.send({ to: "user@example.com", from: { email: "welcome@yourdomain.com", name: "My App" }, // domain must be onboarded subject: "Welcome!", html: "

Welcome!

", text: "Welcome!", // always include text too — spam score + text-only clients }); ``` ## Send — REST API (off Workers) `POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send` with `Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}`. **Field names differ from the binding:** - `from` uses `address` (not `email`): `{ "address": "...", "name": "..." }` - reply address is `reply_to` (snake_case), not `replyTo` - response is `{ delivered: [], permanent_bounces: [], queued: [] }`, not a `messageId` Keep the token in the vault / an env var — never in tracked source. ## Receive — Worker `email()` handler ```typescript export default { async email(message, env, ctx) { // The raw stream is single-use — buffer it ONCE, then reuse: const raw = await new Response(message.raw).arrayBuffer(); // parse with postal-mime, then forward/reply/store await message.forward("team@yourdomain.com"); // destination must be verified }, }; ``` ## Common mistakes | Mistake | Fix | |---------|-----| | No `send_email` binding | Add `"send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }]` — it's a binding, not an API key. | | Sending from an unverified domain | `wrangler email sending enable yourdomain.com` first. | | Reading `message.raw` twice | Single-use stream — buffer once (`await new Response(message.raw).arrayBuffer()`). | | HTML only, no `text` | Always send both `html` and `text`. | | `email` vs `address` in `from` | Binding: `{ email, name }`. REST: `{ address, name }`. | | `replyTo` in REST | REST uses `reply_to` (snake_case). | | Forwarding to an unverified address | `wrangler email routing addresses create user@gmail.com`. | | Testing with fake addresses | Bounces hurt reputation — use real addresses you control. | | Hardcoded API token | Env var / secret, never in source. | | Using it for bulk/marketing | Transactional only — use a marketing platform for campaigns. | ## Deliverability (when in doubt, retrieve) Authenticate the sending domain (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), keep `text` + `html`, honor bounces and suppressions. Full guidance: `https://developers.cloudflare.com/email-service/`. Adjacent skills: `wrangler` (email setup commands), `cloudflare-agents` (agent email handling), `workers-best-practices`.

items.name: Cloudflare Sandbox
items.tagline: Run untrusted or LLM-generated code in isolated Cloudflare Sandbox containers (code interpreter)
items.description: Run untrusted or LLM-generated code in isolated Cloudflare Sandbox containers (code interpreter)
items.readme:
# Cloudflare Sandbox SDK

Secure, isolated execution: each sandbox is a container fronted by a Durable Object, addressed by a
stable id (`getSandbox(env.Sandbox, 'user-123')`). Reach for it when navig-style "let the agent touch
live systems" needs a **blast radius of zero** — untrusted or model-generated code runs in the
sandbox, never on the host.

**Prefer retrieval over memory** — the base image tag and API surface change:
`https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/` (+ `/api/`, `/get-started/`), examples at
`https://github.com/cloudflare/sandbox-sdk/tree/main/examples`.

## First: install (Docker required for local dev)

```bash
npm install @cloudflare/sandbox
docker info   # must succeed — local dev runs the container via Docker
```

## Required config

```jsonc
// wrangler.jsonc — keep this structure
{
  "containers": [{ "class_name": "Sandbox", "image": "./Dockerfile", "instance_type": "lite", "max_instances": 1 }],
  "durable_objects": { "bindings": [{ "class_name": "Sandbox", "name": "Sandbox" }] },
  "migrations": [{ "new_sqlite_classes": ["Sandbox"], "tag": "v1" }]
}
```

```typescript
// Worker entry — the re-export is mandatory or the Worker won't deploy
import { getSandbox } from "@cloudflare/sandbox";
export { Sandbox } from "@cloudflare/sandbox";
```

## Quick reference

| Task | Method |
|------|--------|
| Get a sandbox | `getSandbox(env.Sandbox, 'user-123')` |
| Run a command | `await sandbox.exec('python script.py')` → `{ stdout, stderr, exitCode, success }` |
| Run code (interpreter) | `await sandbox.runCode(code, { language: 'python' })` |
| Write / read file | `await sandbox.writeFile(p, c)` · `await sandbox.readFile(p)` |
| mkdir / list | `await sandbox.mkdir(p, { recursive: true })` · `await sandbox.listFiles(p)` |
| Expose a port | `await sandbox.exposePort(8080)` → `{ url }` |
| Destroy | `await sandbox.destroy()` |

## exec vs runCode

| Need | Use | Why |
|------|-----|-----|
| Shell commands, scripts, build/test | `exec()` | Direct control, exit codes, stderr, streaming |
| LLM-generated code, data analysis | `runCode()` | Rich outputs (charts/tables), **state persists** in a context |

```typescript
// Code interpreter — recommended for AI-generated code
const ctx = await sandbox.createCodeContext({ language: "python" }); // python | javascript | typescript
await sandbox.runCode("import pandas as pd; data = [1,2,3]", { context: ctx });
const r = await sandbox.runCode("sum(data)", { context: ctx }); // r.results[0].text === "6"
```

Create an explicit context in production so state is scoped deliberately.

## Lifecycle

- `getSandbox()` returns immediately; the container starts **lazily** on first operation.
- Idle containers sleep after ~10 min (`sleepAfter`). `destroy()` frees resources now.
- Same `sandboxId` → same instance. Use a **user/session id**, never a hardcoded shared id.

## Extending the image (keep it lean — cold start)

```dockerfile
FROM docker.io/cloudflare/sandbox:0.7.0   # base: Python 3.11, Node 20, common tools
RUN pip install requests beautifulsoup4
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y ffmpeg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
EXPOSE 8080   # required for local-dev port exposure
```

## Preview URLs

`await sandbox.exposePort(8080)` returns a preview URL for an HTTP service inside the sandbox. **In
production this needs a custom domain with wildcard DNS (`*.yourdomain.com`)** — `.workers.dev` does
not serve preview subdomains. See `/sandbox/guides/expose-services/`.

## Anti-patterns

- Don't touch internal clients (`CommandClient`, `FileClient`) — use `sandbox.*`.
- Don't drop the `export { Sandbox }` — deploy fails without it.
- Don't hardcode one sandbox id for multi-user — key by user/session.
- Don't forget `destroy()` on temporary sandboxes.
- Don't trust anything the sandboxed code emits — validate outputs before acting on them.

Adjacent skills: `durable-objects` (the substrate), `cloudflare-agents` (give an agent a sandbox
tool), `workers-best-practices`, `wrangler`.

items.name: Tauri Desktop
items.tagline: Work in a Tauri v2 desktop app (src-tauri/ + Rust + Vite/React) — dev/build, capabilities & IPC, multi-window, the single-instance zombie trap; navig Anchor/Echo/OS
items.description: Work in a Tauri v2 desktop app (src-tauri/ + Rust + Vite/React) — dev/build, capabilities & IPC, multi-window, the single-instance zombie trap; navig Anchor/Echo/OS
items.readme:
# Tauri v2 desktop apps (navig editions)

One web frontend, one Rust backend, one native binary. This skill is the recognition and
workflow layer for navig's Tauri desktop editions. Deep IPC + permission internals live in
[`references/ipc-and-permissions.md`](references/ipc-and-permissions.md) — pull it in when you
add a command, wire a window, or chase a permission-denied error.

## Recognize it

- A **`src-tauri/`** directory: `Cargo.toml`, `tauri.conf.json`, `src/main.rs` (+ usually `lib.rs`
  and a fan of `*_cmd.rs` command modules — Anchor has `neuromancer_cmd.rs`, `command_center.rs`,
  `tools_cmd.rs`, `tray.rs`, …).
- `package.json` with `@tauri-apps/api` **^2** and `@tauri-apps/cli` **^2**.
- A frontend at the repo root: `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/` (React 18 in Anchor/Echo).
- **`src-tauri/capabilities/*.json`** — the v2 permission grants. If this folder exists, treat the
  app as capability-gated (deny-by-default).

The three navig editions, so you scope to the right one:

| App | Path | Identity | Frontend | Package mgr |
|-----|------|----------|----------|-------------|
| **Anchor** | `apps/anchor` | `dev.navig.anchor` — the Neuromancer AI text tool | Vite + React 18 | npm |
| **Echo** | `apps/echo` | voice / inbox / chat | Vite + React | npm |
| **OS** | `apps/os` | the Tauri super-app + browser sidecar | (dashboard) | **Bun** |

Anchor and Echo share the **`shared-desktop`** Rust crate (keystroke layer, window helpers) — a
change there hits both; grep both before editing it.

## Run it — read the scripts first, names drift

```powershell
# Anchor / Echo (npm). "dev" is FRONTEND-ONLY (a browser, no native shell):
npm run dev            # apps/anchor: node scripts/dev.mjs → Vite on :7174, pure UI work
npm run tauri:dev      # full app: builds frontend + Rust, hot-reloads — use for anything native
npm run tauri:build    # release: bundles the installer (.msi/.exe on Windows)
npm run build          # frontend production build (tsc && vite build) — feeds tauri:build

# apps/os is Bun, not npm:
#   bun install ; bun run tauri dev

# Rust-only fast checks, from inside src-tauri/:
cargo check            # type-check the backend without a full build
cargo clippy           # lint
```

Reach for `tauri:dev` whenever you touch a `#[tauri::command]`, a native plugin, or a window —
`npm run dev` alone loads the UI in a plain browser where `invoke(...)` and native APIs don't exist.

## Layout that matters

- **`tauri.conf.json`** — `productName`/`identifier`, the `app.windows[]` array (Anchor runs **nine**
  labelled windows: `palette`, `quickpaste`, `command`, `loupe`, `settings`, `consult`, `manager`,
  `recbar`, `recframe`), the CSP under `app.security`, `bundle` (installer/MSIX metadata), and the
  frontend hooks `build.beforeDevCommand` / `beforeBuildCommand` / `devUrl` / `frontendDist`.
- **`capabilities/default.json`** — lists which **windows** get which **permissions**. This is the
  gate: a native call that isn't granted here fails at runtime, and the Rust code is usually fine.
- **`src/lib.rs`** — the `invoke_handler` registering every Rust command. New command → register here.
- **Rust ↔ JS** — commands (`invoke("cmd", args)` ⇄ `#[tauri::command]`) for request/response; events
  (`emit` ⇄ `listen`) for streaming/async pushes.

## Traps (navig-verified)

- **Single-instance zombie.** Anchor/Echo load the `single-instance` plugin. A crashed or
  still-running `tauri:dev` leaves a stray `NAVIG Anchor.exe` holding the lock and the dev port, so a
  fresh run silently opens no window. Kill it first:
  ```powershell
  Get-Process "NAVIG Anchor" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
  ```
  Use the `productName` from `tauri.conf.json` as the process name. Do this any time "tauri dev does
  nothing."
- **Capabilities deny by default.** A new command or plugin that "doesn't work" is almost always a
  missing grant in `capabilities/default.json` — and for a **new window**, its label must be added to
  that file's `windows` array or none of its permissions apply. See the references file.
- **Two compilers, two failure shapes.** A Rust compile error aborts the whole `tauri:dev` even when
  the frontend is clean. Read which half failed before debugging the wrong side.
- **First release build is slow** (full Rust release compile) — not a hang.
- **Keep JS and Rust versions in lockstep.** Bumping `@tauri-apps/*` npm packages without matching the
  `tauri`/plugin crate versions in `Cargo.toml` produces IPC mismatches.
- **CSP is real.** `app.security.csp` in `tauri.conf.json` blocks anything not allow-listed; a new
  `connect-src`/`img-src` origin (e.g. a provider endpoint) must be added there.
- **OS uses Bun.** Don't `npm install` in `apps/os` — it's excluded from the pnpm workspace and expects
  `bun install`.

## Ship (Anchor → Microsoft Store)

Anchor packages as MSIX via `npm run store:msix` (dry run: `store:msix:dry`, wraps
`scripts/create-msix.ps1`). Bundle identity, publisher, and the long description live in
`tauri.conf.json` `bundle`. The remaining Store blockers are human-only (Partner Center, logos, WACK).

# Next.js App Router apps (navig deck)

The `app/` directory, Server Components by default, Client Components opt-in. This skill recognizes an
App Router project and gives you the conventions to work in one without tripping the server/client
boundary. navig's live example is the **deck** (`apps/deck`) — the Next.js control UI and Telegram
Mini App.

## Recognize it

- An **`app/`** directory with `layout.tsx` + `page.tsx`, and **no** `pages/` directory (that would be
  the legacy Pages Router).
- `next` at **15 or 16**, `react` / `react-dom` at **19** (the deck: Next 16.1.6, React 19.2.4).
- **Tailwind v4** signature: `@tailwindcss/postcss` in devDeps and `@import "tailwindcss";` in
  `app/globals.css` — config lives in CSS via `@theme`, usually **no `tailwind.config.js`**.
- Optional shadcn/ui: `components.json`, `components/ui/*`, a `cn()` helper in `lib/utils.ts`,
  `class-variance-authority` + `tailwind-merge` + `lucide-react`.

Disambiguate: a `src-tauri/` present → **`tauri-desktop`**. Vite + `react-router-dom` (no `app/`) →
**`vite-react-spa`**.

## Run it — read the scripts, ports drift

```powershell
npm install           # or pnpm install
npm run dev           # apps/deck: next dev on :7432 (dev mode = normal Next, so rewrites work)
npm run build         # next build
npm run start         # serve the production build (deck: -p 7432)
npm run lint          # eslint
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit — keep YOUR changed files at zero errors
```

## App Router conventions

- **Routes are folders under `app/`.** A route renders when the folder has a `page.tsx`. The shared
  shell is `app/layout.tsx`; per-segment `loading.tsx` / `error.tsx` / `not-found.tsx` supply the
  streaming, error, and empty states. A new screen = a new `app/<segment>/page.tsx`.
- **Server Components by default; Client Components opt in.** A file is a Server Component unless it
  starts with `"use client"`. Hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`), event handlers, and browser APIs only
  work in client components. Keep the boundary as low in the tree as possible — mark the small
  interactive leaf, not the whole page.
- **Data & mutations.** Route Handlers live at `app/api/<name>/route.ts` (export `GET`/`POST`/…);
  Server Actions are `"use server"` functions callable from a form or a client component. Check which
  exists before wiring a button to it.
- **Styling (Tailwind v4).** Utilities in JSX; theme tokens declared in `globals.css` via `@theme` and
  CSS variables — **not** a JS config. The deck consumes navig design tokens
  (`app/navig-tokens.generated.css`); edit the token source, not the generated file.
- **Path alias.** `@/` → project root (see `tsconfig.json` `paths`).

## navig deck specifics — where the backend actually is

The deck is a **thin control surface over the local daemon**, not a self-contained app:

- In **dev**, `next.config.mjs` runs a normal Next server and **rewrites** `/api/deck/*`,
  `/api/daemon`, `/runtime`, `/mesh`, `/api/events` to the **gateway on `:8789`** (override with
  `NAVIG_DAEMON_URL`). So `npm run dev` talks to an already-running daemon — no second daemon, no CORS
  layer. Don't add a manual proxy; the rewrite is the seam.
- The gateway (default **8789**) serves the deck API + SSE. This is **not** the IPC/MCP daemon (8765) —
  wiring a call to the wrong port is a classic dead end.
- In **build/prod** the deck is a **static export** (`output: "export"`), deployed by a pure-Python
  uploader (`core/navig/cloud/deck_deploy.py`) to Cloudflare Workers Static Assets. The edge brain URL
  is baked in via `NEXT_PUBLIC_LIGHTHOUSE_URL` at build time.

## Traps

- **Server/Client boundary errors.** "useState is not a function" / "cannot be used in a Server
  Component" means a missing `"use client"` — add it to the interactive file, not the whole subtree.
- **Static export constraints.** Because prod is `output: "export"`, features that need a Node server
  at runtime don't apply: `images.unoptimized` is on (no on-the-fly image optimization), and Route
  Handlers/Server Actions won't run on the static edge — dynamic behavior comes from the daemon the
  deck calls, not from Next server code in prod. Verify a data path works **exported**, not just in
  `next dev`.
- **Browser env vars must be `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-prefixed** or they're `undefined` client-side.
- **Tailwind v4 ≠ v3.** No `tailwind.config.js` to edit — customize via `@theme`/CSS variables. Adding
  a v3-style JS config does nothing.
- **shadcn components are yours.** They're copied into `components/ui/*`, editable source — not a
  version-locked dependency. Edit them directly.
- **React 19 peer-dep lag.** Some libraries trail on peer ranges; prefer pinning a compatible version
  over reaching for `--legacy-peer-deps`.

## Publish discipline

The deck is a public surface. When you change what it renders or how it talks to core, update the
relevant `docs/` page and the deck `CHANGELOG.md` in the same change (MASTER § Publish discipline), and
note where the canonical data/route lives so the next agent doesn't guess the port.

items.readme:
# Manifest V3 browser extensions (navig Dock)

An ephemeral service worker, content scripts locked in an isolated world, and a `manifest.json` that
is the whole contract. This skill recognizes an MV3 extension and keeps you on the right side of its
three execution contexts. navig's example is **Dock** (`apps/dock/extension`) — the browser companion
that talks to the local daemon.

## Recognize it

- A **`manifest.json`** with **`"manifest_version": 3`**.
- Keys such as `background.service_worker`, `content_scripts`, `action` (toolbar popup),
  `options_page`/`options_ui`, `permissions`, `host_permissions`, `commands`,
  `web_accessible_resources`, `content_security_policy`.
- A build step: sometimes Vite (`@crxjs/vite-plugin`) or webpack — **Dock uses a custom Node build**
  (`scripts/build.js` with terser + clean-css) that emits `dist/`.
- No bundler at all? The extension folder itself (plain JS/HTML/CSS next to `manifest.json`) is the
  loadable artifact.

Dock's manifest at a glance: `background/service-worker.js` (`type: module`), one content script over
`<all_urls>` at `document_end`, `permissions: [storage, activeTab, tabs, scripting, contextMenus,
alarms]`, `host_permissions` including **`http://localhost:8789/*`** (the local gateway), a `popup`,
an `options_page`, keyboard `commands`, and a lens/apps SDK exposed via `web_accessible_resources`.

## Run it

```powershell
# Dock (custom Node build):
npm install
npm run dev            # scripts/watch.js — rebuild on change
npm run build          # dev build → dist/ (the folder you load)
npm run build:prod     # minified production build
npm run package        # zip dist/ for the store
npm run dev:browser    # launch a browser with the unpacked extension (add :edge for Edge)
```

**Load unpacked (Chrome/Edge):**

1. Open `chrome://extensions` (or `edge://extensions`).
2. Toggle **Developer mode** (top-right).
3. **Load unpacked** → select **`dist/`** (bundled) or the extension root (plain).
4. After edits: click **Reload** on the card. Manifest or service-worker changes *require* a card
   reload; content-script changes also need the **target page refreshed**.

## Three contexts — never confuse them

| Context | Where it runs | Sees | Key limits |
|---------|---------------|------|-----------|
| **Service worker** (`background.service_worker`) | extension, headless | no DOM | **event-driven, can die anytime** — hold no long-lived memory, persist to `chrome.storage`; register listeners at top level so they survive restart |
| **Content script** (`content_scripts` / `chrome.scripting`) | inside the page | the page DOM | **isolated world** — cannot read the page's JS globals; only a slim `chrome.*` surface (messaging + storage) |
| **Popup / options** | extension page | its own DOM | full `chrome.*` access |

**Messaging bridges them:** `chrome.runtime.sendMessage` / `onMessage` between popup ⇄ worker;
`chrome.tabs.sendMessage` to reach a content script. UI ↔ worker ↔ page communicate only through
messages — there is no shared memory.

## Manifest is the contract

A new content script, `command`, icon, permission, or web-exposed file must be declared in
`manifest.json` or it does not exist at runtime. Keep permissions least-privilege: `permissions`
(API access) and `host_permissions` (which sites) are separate, and MV3 prefers `activeTab` +
`chrome.scripting` over a broad host grant. Files the page must load (Dock's lens/app SDK) go in
`web_accessible_resources`.

## Traps

- **The service worker is not persistent.** MV3 killed background pages — any variable in the worker
  can vanish between events. Persist to `chrome.storage.local`/`session`; re-register `onMessage` /
  `onAlarm` listeners at the top level, never inside an async callback.
- **Content scripts can't touch the page's JS.** Isolated world: you see the DOM, not the site's
  `window` globals. To reach page-world variables, inject a `<script>` into the page and talk via
  `window.postMessage` / DOM events.
- **Reload discipline is the #1 "my change didn't work."** Manifest/worker edit → card **Reload**;
  content-script edit → **also refresh the page**. With `@crxjs`, HMR reloads scripts for you but a
  manifest change may still need a manual card reload.
- **Extension CSP is strict** — no remote scripts, no `eval`, no inline handlers on extension pages.
  Bundle everything locally (Dock's `content_security_policy.extension_pages` enforces `script-src
  'self'`).
- **MV2 patterns are dead** — no `background.scripts`/persistent page, `browser_action` → `action`,
  blocking `webRequest` → `declarativeNetRequest`. Don't port MV2 snippets verbatim.
- **navig-specific: the shared page-bar contract.** Dock's on-page bar coordinates with a sibling
  extension's bar through a `data-webbar-*` DOM contract (tri-state auto-position) so the two don't
  overlap. Don't hardcode a position or assume Dock owns the page edge — honor the shared attributes.
- **navig-specific: gateway reachability.** Dock's live features call the local daemon at
  `http://localhost:8789` (a declared `host_permission`). If integration goes dead, confirm the daemon
  is running and the host grant is still in the manifest before touching extension code.

items.readme:
# Web performance audit (Chrome DevTools MCP)

Measure first, recommend only what the trace proves. This skill drives the **`chrome-devtools`** MCP
server to record a real page load, then reads the numbers and the code behind them. Thresholds and
tooling drift — **prefer live retrieval over memory** for any specific number you cite.

The full tool table, phased workflow, insight names, and threshold table live in
[`references/devtools-mcp.md`](references/devtools-mcp.md). This page is the router and the
house rules.

## Step 0 — verify the MCP server (do this first)

Try calling `navigate_page` or `performance_start_trace`. If they aren't available, **stop** — the
`chrome-devtools` MCP server isn't configured. Ask the user to add it:

```json
"chrome-devtools": { "type": "local", "command": ["npx", "-y", "chrome-devtools-mcp@latest"] }
```

## The audit, in five phases

Track it as a checklist:

```
- [ ] 1. Trace       — navigate + record a cold load (reload: true)
- [ ] 2. Web Vitals  — LCP / INP / CLS breakdowns, CLS culprits
- [ ] 3. Network     — render-blocking, late chains, caching, oversized payloads
- [ ] 4. A11y        — accessibility-tree snapshot, contrast, names, focus
- [ ] 5. Code        — framework/bundler + tree-shaking/compression (skip for third-party sites)
```

Retrieval sources when you need current numbers: web.dev/articles/vitals (vitals thresholds),
developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/performance (tooling), the Lighthouse scoring page (weights).
See the references file for the per-metric good / needs-improvement / poor bands.

## House rules — be assertive, quantify, prioritize

- **Verify, then state definitively.** Confirm a resource is unused (zero requests to that origin)
  before recommending removal; confirm a claim against the network log or DOM, then say it plainly.
- **Quantify impact.** Use the estimated savings the insight reports. Don't recommend a change with
  0ms impact — note it and move on.
- **Be specific.** "Convert `hero.png` (450 KB) to WebP and set explicit width/height" beats "optimize
  images."
- **Prioritize ruthlessly.** A page at 200ms LCP and 0 CLS is already excellent — say so and stop. Rank
  findings High / Medium / Low by measured effect.
- **Don't weaken the target to score.** No suppressing a real regression, no gaming a metric that
  hides a genuine UX cost.

## navig surfaces

- **The deck (`apps/deck`)** ships as a **static export** on Cloudflare Workers Static Assets, so it
  starts with edge-served static HTML/JS and strong cache headers — LCP is usually dominated by the JS
  bundle and first data call to the daemon, and CLS by late-mounting panels. Audit the exported build,
  not `next dev` (dev has no minification/caching and will lie about prod).
- **The marketing site (www)** is a public, first-impression surface — LCP (hero image/font), CLS
  (web-font swap, un-sized media), and cache headers are the usual wins.

## Output format

1. **Core Web Vitals summary** — a table: metric · value · rating (good / needs-improvement / poor).
2. **Top issues** — prioritized (High/Medium/Low) with the measured impact for each.
3. **Recommendations** — specific, actionable, with the concrete file/config change.
4. **Codebase findings** — framework + bundler detected and the optimization openings (omit if you had
   no codebase access).

# Vite + React SPA (± Express)

A client-rendered React app that Vite builds, often with a thin Express server behind a shared, typed
contract. This skill recognizes the shape fast and — crucially — reads **past** identical starter
scaffolding to the app's real intent. It covers both the pure-frontend SPA and the full-stack
`client/server/shared` variant.

## Recognize it

- **`vite.config.ts`** (or `.js`) + an **`index.html`** entry + `react` / `react-dom` in
  `package.json`. That's the SPA baseline.
- Client-side routing via **`react-router-dom`** (a route table in `App.tsx`/`main.tsx`) — an SPA, not
  file-system routing.
- **Full-stack variant:** top-level `client/`, `server/`, `shared/` dirs side by side; `express` in
  deps; a `vite.config.ts` that mounts the Express app as dev middleware; often TanStack Query + Zod,
  a `@radix-ui/*`/shadcn cluster, and an `AGENTS.md` instead of a `README.md`.

Disambiguate: an `app/` dir with Next → **`nextjs-app`**. A `src-tauri/` → **`tauri-desktop`** (the
navig Anchor/Echo frontends *are* Vite + React, but wrapped by Tauri — use that skill for the native
side; the Vite patterns here still apply to their UI).

## Run it — read `package.json` scripts first (names drift)

```bash
npm install           # or pnpm install
npm run dev           # Vite dev server (full-stack variant: Vite + Express on ONE port)
npm run build         # production build (client + server bundle in the full-stack variant)
npm start             # run the built server (full-stack) / preview the build
npm test              # Vitest, if present
npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit (sometimes "type-check")
```

In the full-stack variant there is **no separate backend port** in dev — Express runs *inside* Vite as
middleware, so `/api/*` calls hit the same origin with no proxy and no CORS layer. Don't add one; check
`vite.config.ts` first.

## Where things live

| Concern | Pure SPA | Full-stack (`client/server/shared`) |
|---------|----------|-------------------------------------|
| Pages | `src/pages/*` | `client/pages/*` |
| Components | `src/components/*` (`ui/` = shadcn primitives) | `client/components/*` |
| Route table | `src/App.tsx` / `main.tsx` | `client/App.tsx` |
| API handlers | — | `server/` (Express app + routes; `server/index.ts` exports the app) |
| Shared contract | — | `shared/` — types + Zod schemas imported by **both** sides |
| Path alias | `@/` → `src/` | `@/` → `client/`, `@shared/` → `shared/` (check `tsconfig.json` + `vite.config.ts`) |

- **Routing** is a React Router table — a new screen is a `pages/*` file wired into it.
- **Data fetching** — TanStack Query on the client; validate payloads with the Zod schemas from
  `shared/` so the client and server agree on shape.
- **Styling** — Tailwind (v3 with a `tailwind.config.ts` `content` glob, or v4 config-in-CSS) plus CSS
  variables for theming.

## Traps

- **Don't trust the scaffolding — derive intent from the code.** Cloned starters (Builder.io Fusion,
  bootstrap templates) share identical files, names, and `AGENTS.md` across many repos; the template
  metadata tells you nothing about *this* app. Read the actual `pages/*` and `server/routes/*` to learn
  what it does. Two repos off the same starter are not related.
- **`AGENTS.md` over a missing README.** Many starters ship guidance in `AGENTS.md` and no `README.md` —
  read it before assuming conventions.
- **The Express server is often half-wired** in prototypes — endpoints may be stubs. Confirm a route
  exists in `server/` before calling it from the client.
- **One origin in dev.** Don't add a manual proxy or CORS expecting a split front/back — the Vite
  middleware serves both.
- **Keep new routes in `server/`** so both the dev middleware and any deploy wrapper (a Netlify/edge
  function importing the same Express app) pick them up — don't duplicate a handler in the function
  entry.
- **SPA routing needs a fallback.** A client-routed build serves `index.html` for unknown paths; a
  static host without a rewrite-to-index rule will 404 on deep links — configure the fallback.
